title: UF President Bell Says H-1B Filing Was Posted Without His Approval, Removes It
excerpt: The removed filing sought a financial analyst at about $65,000 starting February 2027, weeks after Florida's pause on new university H-1B hires expires.
body:
• University of Florida President Stuart Bell said an H-1B filing for a financial analyst was posted without his approval or authorization and has been removed.
  • The filing sought a Financial Analyst II at $64,928, based at 33 Tigert Hall, for February 2, 2027 to February 1, 2030.
  • Florida's Board of Governors has paused new H-1B hires at public universities until January 5, 2027; existing contracts need not be terminated and renewals remain allowed.
  • For international staff and students in Florida: the pause covers new hires only — current H-1B holders at UF, which approved 253 H-1B visas in fiscal 2025, can still renew during the pause.

University of Florida President Stuart Bell said an H-1B visa filing seeking to hire a financial analyst was made without his approval and has been removed, the Gainesville Sun reported. The removal came amid a statewide pause on new H-1B hires at Florida public universities.

"This job was posted without my approval or authorization, and it has been removed. The University of Florida will continue to remain in full compliance with Governor DeSantis' direction on H-1B hires."

— Stuart Bell, President, University of Florida

How the filing surfaced

Bell's comments followed an October 27 post on X by Chris Brunet, a former contributing editor at The American Conservative who now runs an online newsletter. Brunet published details of the filing, including a salary of about $65,000 and a copy of the filing itself, according to the Sun. In his own account, Brunet put the salary at $64,928.75 for a Financial Analyst II, with a posting date of October 26, 2026 and a requested employment period beginning February 2, 2027 — less than a month after the Florida pause expires.

The filing listed the worksite as 33 Tigert Hall in Gainesville, home to the university's Division of Contracts and Grants, and an employment period running to February 1, 2030. Brunet's post was also shared under an October 24 post by Governor Ron DeSantis, who wrote that Florida had stopped H-1Bs at its universities and that other states should follow suit. University officials told the Sun they had no further comment.

The statewide pause behind the dispute

The Florida Board of Governors voted on March 2 to pause the hiring of new employees on H-1B visas until January 5, 2027, after DeSantis accused state universities of favoring foreign workers over US citizens. The H-1B program allows US employers to hire foreign professionals with highly specialized knowledge and at least a bachelor's degree for up to six years. Under the Board's vote, universities are not required to terminate existing contracts, and current H-1B visas may still be renewed during the pause.

That distinction matters at UF more than at any other Florida public university. The university employs the largest number of H-1B holders among the state's public universities, according to previous reporting by The Independent Florida Alligator cited by the Sun. US Citizenship and Immigration Services data show UF approved 253 H-1B visas, including new and renewed visas, in fiscal year 2025, and had approved 57 more in the first two months of 2026.

An oversight question, not just a posting

Bell took the filing at face value as unauthorized, and Brunet said he welcomed that response. But Brunet also raised the question the episode leaves open in his account of the removal: a university with administrators, lawyers and an immigration compliance office published a federal hiring notice that its president says he never approved. How it reached publication, and whether internal controls change as a result, has not been explained. UF offered no further comment to the Sun.

What happens next

The filing itself is gone, so no hire will proceed from it. The broader pause runs until January 5, 2027, and the requested start date in the removed filing — February 2, 2027 — fell just after that expiry, a timing that will keep scrutiny on university filings as the deadline approaches. For now, Florida's public universities remain barred from new H-1B hires, while renewals for existing staff continue.
